adoption.notes: In v2.5.0-rc.10 and v2.5.0-rc.11 the HTTP exporter admitted only events typed sensor.reading while the poll loop and the firmware subscriber publish a reading as sensor.<sensor_type>, so it queued no reading unless a sensor's type was reading. From 2045efd it admits both and still writes sensor.reading in the batch. Neither has been exercised against a live receiver.

hunks.summary: The blank quoted lines that close the generated Status paragraph and separate the Supersedes and Primary consumer notes; formatting only.

A record's receipt is the moment it was first stored and a replay does not move it, and the Producer Time section: a receiver keeps a producer timestamp as reported, never ranks records by one, lets one make a record older but never newer, and shows it as reported under its own name. These are new receiver obligations. Restored out of v2.
A producer has at most one reading batch in flight. A new producer obligation. Restored out of v2.
last_success_ms becomes required for reading and failing and never null, where v2 had "Only when known". A tightened rule. Restored out of v2.
sent_at_ms is no longer the sensor-status ordering key: a receiver keeps the snapshot it most recently accepted, and must not compare the two clocks. A changed receiver rule. Restored out of v2.

The rejection reasons a receiver may give are not a closed set, a member outside the table's form refuses the snapshot whole, and a producer must not treat an unrecognised reason as malformed. New obligations on both parties. Restored out of v2.

A rejected entry supersedes what was held for that sensor; sensors is never empty and a receiver refuses an empty array; a superseded state is not recoverable. New receiver obligations and a new refusal. Restored out of v2.

notes: The ingest consumer is outside the repositories these records track. The exporter states that delivery "follows" this contract, which does not state conformance; the version freezes by shipment in v2.5.0-rc.10.
